Unofficial integration, not affiliated with Octopus Energy. It reads your
**Octopus Energy Germany** customer account through the official Kraken API
of Octopus Germany (`api.oeg-kraken.energy`, documented on
developer.oeg-kraken.energy) and gives Gladys:

- one device per **electricity market location (MaLo)** of the account, with
  the price per kWh now, the next price, the monthly standing charge and, for
  a smart meter (iMSys), the consumption by half hour for the energy
  monitoring;
- one device per **Intelligent Octopus device** (car, charge point) with
  "Smart charge planned now";
- an energy contract template, **Octopus Energy Germany electricity**, priced
  from the tariff of your account: fixed, time-of-use (Intelligent Octopus
  Go, Heat…) or dynamic.

**Read-only.** The only request that is not a read is the login. Nothing is
ever changed on your account, your meters or your devices (no smart charge,
no boost, no meter reading sent).

> This integration has never been tested with a real Octopus Germany account:
> it was written from the published API schema and from the queries of
> octopus_germany (Home Assistant, MIT). Please report what you see.

## Setup

1. **Recommended: an API key** of your Octopus account (`sk_live_…`). It is
   the durable way to log in; if you have none, ask Octopus customer service.
   It is used alone when given.
2. **Fallback: the e-mail address and the password** of the Octopus website
   and app. Kraken marked this login deprecated in 2026 (removal announced
   "on or after 2026-09-21"); it still worked in October 2026. When Octopus
   stops accepting it, the status says so and asks for an API key.
   Whatever you enter is kept by Gladys in its database, the secrets never
   shown again, and sent only to Octopus Germany to log in. The integration
   keeps the Kraken token in memory only.
3. With several accounts on one login, enter the **account number** to read
   (empty: the first one; the status says so).
4. Press **Test the connection** (at most once a minute): it logs in and
   counts your accounts.
5. In **Discovery**, add the devices you want. Nothing is asked of Octopus
   for a device nobody added (consumption, planned charges).
6. In the energy settings of Gladys, create a contract from the template
   **Octopus Energy Germany electricity** on your meter: enter the last 4
   digits of the MaLo (shown in the device name; may be left empty only with
   a single MaLo: with several, an empty or ambiguous value is refused) and
   your monthly standing charge (shown by the "Standing charge per month"
   feature, VAT included).

## Devices

| Device                           | Feature                   | Meaning                                         |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Octopus electricity (MaLo …1234) | Price per kWh now         | gross price (VAT included), EUR/kWh             |
|                                  | Next price per kWh        | the next different price within 2 days          |
|                                  | Standing charge per month | gross, EUR, from your agreement                 |
|                                  | Consumption (30 min)      | smart meter (iMSys) only, kWh, dated by Octopus |
| Octopus Intelligent …            | Smart charge planned now  | 1 inside a planned charge, 0 outside            |

The **device id** is a keyed hash of the MaLo number (HMAC-SHA-256, 16 hex
digits) under a random key made at the first start and kept by Gladys in the
integration config, outside the form (never in `/data`): without that key,
neither the id nor `/data` gives the MaLo back, even with its last 4 digits,
which the device name shows. Until Gladys has stored that key, nothing is
read nor published (status "Gladys could not store the key…", tried again
with the next read of the account: after 5, 10, 20, 40 then every 60
minutes; saving the form tries again too, at most once in 5 s, doubled up
to 5 minutes). The MaLo number itself never appears in an id,
a log, the status or `/data`. The MaLo, not the meter, is the identity: a
replaced meter keeps its Gladys device and its history.

A value Octopus does not give stays unknown: nothing is ever published as 0
in its place. The prices are published again at every quarter of an hour
from what was read; a tariff read more than 6 hours ago is not published as
current any more.

## Pace

- the account (tariffs, dynamic prices ahead, devices): every hour;
- the consumption of the added meters: every 3 hours, the last 3 days; 7
  days for a new device and once a day after 06:00 (German time);
- the planned charges of the added Intelligent devices: every 15 minutes.

Each time is kept in `/data` before the request: a restart, a reconnection or
Discovery never bring a read forward, and the test button only logs in and
lists the accounts (at most once a minute). Two exceptions, a minute after
the previous read at the earliest: another login or account number saved in
the form (the account), a meter device just added (its consumption). The
requests go one at a time, 2 seconds apart.

## The energy contract

The template is **priced by the integration** (delegated): Gladys sends the
consumption by half hour, the integration answers its cost:

- the price of a half hour is the mean of its two quarters of an hour, VAT
  included, from the agreement in force then (a change of tariff mid-month is
  priced right);
- **dynamic tariff**: the price of the Octopus forecast for that quarter,
  nothing else; **time-of-use** (Intelligent Octopus Go: 00:00 to 05:00 German
  time): the rate of the time slot, the changes of time included;
  **fixed**: the rate, within the dates Octopus gives it;
- a negative price costs 0 (Gladys does not take credits);
- an unknown price is never a 0: the whole request of Gladys fails (up to a
  month of half hours), and Gladys asks again later. Its catch-up starts from
  the oldest half hour without a cost and covers 31 days: one quarter of an
  hour without a known price keeps the rest of that billing period without a
  cost until the quarter leaves this window.

A dynamic tariff is priced from its forecast only, never from the fixed rate
of the product: an agreement seen dynamic once stays so (kept in `/data`),
and an answer of Octopus carrying an error (for example KT-CT-3956 on the
forecast) only spoils the part it points at (that agreement has no price, that
MaLo keeps what was read before); an error pointing nowhere spoils the whole
answer, a passing error: nothing is taken from it, the prices read
before are kept. The dynamic prices are only known ahead of time (today and
tomorrow): the integration keeps every price it has seen in `/data` for 40
days, so that it can price the past, and a price kept for a quarter already
started is never rewritten. **Start the contract on the day the integration
was installed** (or later), and keep Gladys running: a quarter of an hour it
never saw ahead has no known dynamic price (see above).

Not included: a variable §14a grid fee (module 3), which Octopus bills on top
for the customers who chose it. The standing charge is the amount you enter
in the contract (Gladys computes it, not the integration).

## Status and errors

| Status                                                     | Meaning                                                                                                                                                     | What happens                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Octopus refused the login (KT-CT-1138, 1134 or 1135)       | the login refused: wrong e-mail, password or API key (1134 and 1135 are documented for refresh tokens; answered to this login, they are taken as a refusal) | no request until you change the credentials or Test succeeds (another account number alone does not lift it) |
| API access is not enabled (KT-CT-11334)                    | Octopus disabled API access for this user                                                                                                                   | same                                                                                                         |
| Octopus no longer accepts the login by e-mail and password | the schema refuses these fields, or KT-CT-1113                                                                                                              | pause of 1 hour, doubled up to 6 hours; lifted by an API key                                                 |
| Octopus blocks the login for now (KT-CT-1136)              | a temporary block, seen with valid credentials                                                                                                              | pause of 1 hour, doubled up to 6 hours                                                                       |
| Octopus asked to slow down                                 | HTTP 429 or KT-CT-1199                                                                                                                                      | pause of Retry-After or 15 minutes, doubled up to 6 hours                                                    |
| Octopus is having trouble                                  | HTTP 5xx or KT-CT-7899                                                                                                                                      | pause of 5 minutes, doubled up to 6 hours                                                                    |
| Octopus could not be read                                  | network, timeout, unreadable or partial answer, a query refused                                                                                             | tried again after 5, 10, 20, 40 then every 60 minutes                                                        |

A 401 or 403 answered to a query (not to the login) is never taken as a
refused password: one new login, then a passing error. The pauses and the
refusal are kept in `/data` (the refusal as 8 bits of a salted hash of the
credentials, never the credentials).

**Octopus' new sign-in.** If the website accepts your password but the
integration says it is refused, your account may use the new sign-in: an API
key of the account still works (ask Octopus for one).

## What `/data` holds

`/data/octopus-germany.json`: the time of the last reads, the pause, the
refusal (8 bits of a salted hash), the MaLos seen (at most 8: keyed hash,
last 4 digits, tariff name, smart meter or not, when last seen), the
agreements seen dynamic (keyed hash) and the prices of the last 40 days.
Never the e-mail address, the password, a token, the id key, the account
number nor a whole MaLo number.

## Limits

- Electricity only: gas, feed-in (export) and the balance of the account are
  not read.
- The planned charges of Intelligent Octopus do not change the price
  computed here: the tariff time slots do.
- Never tested with a real account (see above): the answers are read
  strictly, and an answer of an unexpected shape is a passing error, never a
  wrong value.

## Credits

The GraphQL queries are adapted from octopus_germany by thecem (MIT,
github.com/thecem/octopus_germany), as is the reading of the tariffs and of
the measurements, rewritten in JavaScript. Notice in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Octopus Energy Germany asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Octopus Energy Germany account | `section` | No | Unofficial connector, not affiliated with Octopus Energy. For Octopus Energy customers in Germany. Recommended: an API key of your Octopus account (sk_live_…, ask Octopus customer service if you have none). The e-mail address and password of the Octopus website still work as a fallback, but Kraken deprecated that login in 2026 and may remove it. The integration reads your electricity market locations (MaLo), their tariff (fixed, time-of-use such as Intelligent Octopus Go, or dynamic), the smart-meter consumption (iMSys) for the Gladys energy monitoring and the smart charges planned for your Intelligent devices. Read-only: nothing is ever changed on your account. Then create an energy contract from the "Octopus Energy Germany electricity" template. |
| API key (recommended) | `secret` | No | An API key of your Octopus account (sk_live_…): the durable way to log in, used alone when given. Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only to Octopus Energy Germany. |
| E-mail address (fallback) | `string` | No | Without an API key: the e-mail address you log in with on the Octopus website (a login Kraken deprecated in 2026). |
| Password (fallback) | `secret` | No | Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only to Octopus Energy Germany (api.oeg-kraken.energy) to log in. |
| Account number (optional) | `string` | No | Only needed when your login has several Octopus accounts: empty, the first one is read. |

## How to install Octopus Energy Germany in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Octopus Energy Germany appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-octopus-germany:0.1.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-octopus-germany](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-octopus-germany).

Octopus Energy Germany requires Gladys `>=5.3.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Octopus Energy Germany is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core.
